questions.question: Since 1 May 2026, can a landlord in England end a tenancy with a no-fault section 21 notice?
questions.explanation: The Renters' Rights Act ended no-fault section 21 evictions in England. A landlord now needs a legal ground.
questions.verify: Renters' Rights Act changes from 1 May 2026

questions.question: New tenancies in England now usually have…
options: A rolling tenancy with no fixed end date
questions.explanation: New tenancies are rolling (periodic) with no fixed end date.

questions.question: To leave a rolling tenancy, how much written notice does a tenant give?
questions.explanation: A tenant can leave by giving 2 months' written notice, on the rent day or the day before.

questions.question: A landlord who wants you out of your home now needs…
options: A legal ground and usually 4 months' notice
questions.explanation: A landlord needs a legal ground and usually gives 4 months' notice, though some grounds allow less.

questions.question: How often can a landlord raise the rent in a rolling tenancy?
options: Once a year, and not in the first 12 months
questions.explanation: Rent can go up once a year, and not in the first 12 months.

questions.question: What must a landlord use to propose a rent increase?
options: The official Form 4A with at least 2 months' notice
questions.explanation: They must use the official form (Form 4A) and give at least 2 months' notice. You can challenge an increase above market rent.

questions.question: A property is advertised at £1,200 a month. Can the landlord accept a bid of £1,300?
options: Yes, if it is paid up front
No, they cannot accept offers above the advertised rent
Yes, if it is the highest bid
questions.explanation: Adverts must state a specific price, and landlords cannot accept or encourage offers above it.

questions.question: After the tenancy agreement is signed, a landlord can ask for at most how much rent in advance?
questions.explanation: Landlords cannot ask for rent before signing. After signing, they can ask for at most 1 month's rent in advance.

questions.question: Can a landlord refuse to rent to you because you receive benefits or have children?
questions.explanation: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you because you receive benefits or have children.

questions.question: A Rent Repayment Order can require a landlord to repay up to how much rent?
questions.explanation: For some offences, such as letting a property that should be licensed, tenants can apply for an order requiring repayment of up to 2 years' rent.

questions.question: In England, a tenancy deposit is capped at how many weeks' rent (for annual rent under £50,000)?
questions.explanation: The cap is 5 weeks' rent, or 6 weeks if the annual rent is £50,000 or more.

questions.question: A holding deposit is capped at…
questions.explanation: A holding deposit is capped at 1 week's rent, and only one can be taken for a property at a time.

questions.question: Within how many days must a landlord protect a tenancy deposit in an approved scheme?
questions.explanation: The deposit must be protected in a government-approved scheme within 30 days of receiving it.

questions.question: If the tenancy goes ahead, the holding deposit must usually be returned within…
questions.explanation: The holding deposit must usually be returned within 7 days, whether the tenancy goes ahead or the landlord decides not to proceed.

questions.question: A landlord can only charge a late-rent fee once rent is at least how overdue?
questions.explanation: A late-rent fee is only allowed once rent is at least 14 days overdue, and it is capped.

questions.question: An agent asks you to pay a £150 reference check fee. Is that allowed in England?
options: No, reference check fees are banned
Yes, it is a normal charge
questions.explanation: Reference check fees and other charges for granting a tenancy are banned.

questions.question: Councils can fine landlords up to how much for a first breach of the fee rules?
questions.explanation: Councils can fine up to £5,000 for a first breach, and up to £30,000 for a repeat breach within 5 years.

questions.question: What is the best way to pay a deposit so you can prove it later?
questions.explanation: Pay by a method you can prove, such as bank transfer, and keep receipts.

questions.question: You cannot pay rent this month. What should you do first?
options: Tell your landlord or agent as early as you can
questions.explanation: Tell them early, ask what can be agreed in writing, and get free help from Shelter, Citizens Advice or MoneyHelper.

questions.question: You set up a standing order for your rent. Who sets it up?
questions.explanation: A standing order is set up by you with your bank. A Direct Debit is set up by the landlord, who collects the payment.

questions.question: Does paying rent normally appear on your credit file?
questions.explanation: Normally, paying rent does not appear on your credit file. Rent reporting services aim to change that.

questions.question: If a rent reporting service reports your payments, must lenders use that data?
questions.explanation: Lenders do not have to use rent data, and many do not, so a score change is not guaranteed.

questions.question: What does Open Banking let a rent reporting service do?
options: See your rent payments with read-only access
questions.explanation: The service asks for read-only access to your bank transactions, finds your rent payments and reports them.

questions.question: A service gives 1 point per £1 of rent, and 100 points = £1. About what do you get back on £1,000 rent?
questions.explanation: 1,000 points at 100 points per £1 is £10, about 1%. Always check the current rate and fees.

questions.question: A rent-by-card service charges 1.99%. On £1,000 of rent, what is the fee?
questions.explanation: 1.99% of £1,000 is £19.90. Card rewards must beat that for it to make sense.

questions.question: You pay rent by credit card and do not clear the balance. What is the risk?
options: Interest can cost more than the rewards
questions.explanation: If you do not clear the card in full by the due date, interest can cost more than any rewards.

questions.question: Why check that rewards are worth it before changing how you pay rent?
options: Rewards are often small and terms change
questions.explanation: The rewards are usually small and terms change often, so work out the real value first.
